title: Feature/playlist editor redesign
summary: Since the last plan (commit `6a6cdd9`), the editor became one three-screen flow (details, steps, review) used on both computers and phones, scenes and "Test with a group" were removed, "Who can open it" moved to the details screen with three choices, questions got an optional author's answer, compare steps use the passage picker, playlists are saved in a shape older versions of Seed Bible can still read, and playing on a phone got a slimmer layout. As a whole, this pull request redesigns how playlists are made and played: a fullscreen editor, new step types (notes, questions, side-by-side compares, videos), fullscreen step screens while playing, a group mode where the leader moves everyone on, a completion screen, and a "Continue your playlist" card on Today. The pull request has no description, so the tests below follow what the app does.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the window at full width. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email: Seed Bible emails you a code, so you need an inbox you can check. Saving and publishing a playlist needs an account. If you can, use an account that already has playlists made before this change: one test checks they still open.

setup.title: Find the Discover pane
setup.body: Open **Discover** from the app's menu. This is where playlists are listed, created and played. Every test below starts from here unless it says otherwise.

tests.title: Older playlists still show and play
tests.why: A reviewer reported on the earlier commit that their existing playlists failed to load with an error ("Failed to sync playlists"). Commit `1acce9d` changes how playlists are stored so that older playlists keep loading, and one broken playlist no longer hides the whole list.
steps: In **Discover**, look at your list of playlists.
Open a playlist that was made before this change (one of yours, or one in Discover) and play it from start to finish.
expected: All your earlier playlists are listed; none are missing and no error appears.
Every step plays, nothing is missing or shown as an unknown type, and the completion screen appears at the end.

sections.title: Making a playlist on a computer
sections.intro: The fullscreen editor, in three screens: details, steps, and review.

tests.title: A new playlist starts on its details screen
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: a new playlist used to open straight on the steps; it now asks for its details first, and "Who can open it" lives here.
steps: In **Discover**, choose **+ Create**, then **Playlist**.
Look at the screen that opens.
Type `Test playlist` in **Title** and a short description in **Description**.
Under **Who can open it**, choose **Anyone with a link**.
Choose **Next**.
expected: A fullscreen screen headed **New playlist** shows **Title**, **Description**, **Cover image** and **Who can open it**, with a **Next** button.

**Who can open it** offers three choices: **Only me** ("Keep it as a draft for yourself"), **Me and my friends** ("Your friends see it in Discover"), and **Anyone with a link** ("Only people you send the link to"). **Me and my friends** is chosen at first.

**Next** opens the steps screen: **Steps** on the left, "Pick a step on the left, or add one." in the middle, and **Step settings** on the right. The header shows the title, a cover thumbnail, **Edit** / **Preview** buttons and **Review & publish**.
There is no **Test with a group** button any more.

tests.title: Add a scripture step by typing a reference
tests.before: Keep the editor from the previous test open.
steps: Choose **Add step** at the bottom of the Steps column.
In the **Add a step** window, leave **Scripture** selected under "1 · Step type".
Under "2 · Passage", type `John 3:16-18`.
Choose **Add step**.
expected: While you type, the window shows the chapter's verses with 16–18 marked, and the bottom of the window says something like "Scripture · John 3:16-18 · 3 verses".
The window closes and **John 3:16-18** appears as step 1 in the Steps column, opened in the middle column.
The Steps column heading shows the step count and an estimated time (for example "1 · ~1 min").

tests.title: Pick a passage by dragging across verses
steps: Choose **Add step** again, keep **Scripture**.
Type `Psalm 23` so the chapter's text shows, then press and drag from verse 1 to verse 3 in the text.
Choose **Add step**.
expected: The dragged verses are selected and the reference box updates to Psalm 23:1-3.
Step 2 is added after step 1.

tests.title: Add one of each other step type
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: Compare now picks each passage with the same passage picker as Scripture, Question has an optional answer, Note + Scripture no longer has a "+ Question" button, and Add scene is gone.
steps: Add a **Note** step: choose **Add step**, pick **Note**, type `A short note for readers`, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Note + Scripture** step: pick it, type the passage `Romans 8:28`, type a note title and a short note, choose **Add step**.
Add a **Compare** step: pick it, enter `Genesis 1:1` as the first passage, then choose the second passage's tab and enter `John 1:1`. Choose **Add step**.
Add a **Question** step: pick it, type `What stood out to you?` as the question and `That God loves the world.` in **Your answer (optional)**. Choose **Add step**.
Add a **Link** step with the address `https://example.com`.
Add a **Video** step with any YouTube video address, and leave the **Transcript** box empty.
expected: Each type's window shows the right fields. Compare shows two tabs, one per passage, each with the passage picker (a reference box plus the chapter's text). Note + Scripture has no **+ Question** button.
Fields are a sensible size: a one-line title box is one line tall, not half the window.
Each new step appears in the Steps column with an icon or label that matches its type, numbered in order.
The bottom of the Steps column has **Add step** only, no **Add scene**.

tests.title: Compare needs both passages
steps: Choose **Add step**, pick **Compare**, enter only `Genesis 1:1` as the first passage.
Choose **Add step** without filling in the second passage.
expected: The step isn't added. The window says "Choose both passages to compare" and switches to the empty passage's tab.
Close the window without adding the step.

tests.title: Move steps by dragging and with the keyboard
tests.why: New since commit `6a6cdd9`: dragging used to jump two places for every one the pointer moved, and the drag handle now also works with the arrow keys.
steps: In the Steps column, drag the last step slowly upward by its drag handle, past two or three steps, and let go.
Click the drag handle of any step once, then press the Up arrow key twice and the Down arrow key once.
expected: While dragging, the step stays under your pointer and lands where you let go.
Each arrow press moves that step one place, and the handle stays selected so you can keep pressing.

tests.title: Step settings: reading time, group options and changing type
steps: Open step 1 (John 3:16-18) in the Steps column.
Under **Reading time**, note the estimate and the word "auto", then choose **edit**, type `5`, and press Enter.
Choose **Use the estimate**.
Tick **Leader only (hide from solo readers)** and **Pause here for discussion**.
Under **Type**, choose **Note + Scripture**.
expected: After typing 5, reading time shows 5 min and the Steps column's total time goes up. **Use the estimate** puts it back to the estimate with "auto".
The ticks stay ticked when you open another step and come back.

Choosing a different type opens a window titled **Change the step's type**; after you finish it, the step keeps its place, its reading time and both ticks, and the middle column shows the new type's editor straight away.

tests.title: Same passage twice in a row is flagged
steps: Add a new **Scripture** step for exactly the same passage as the step before it (for example `Psalm 23:1-3` right after Psalm 23:1-3).
Look at **Step settings** for the new step.
Choose **Remove step N** in the warning.
expected: A warning says "Same passage as step N" and "Readers will see Psalm 23:1-3 twice in a row. This step already shows it."
**Remove step N** removes the earlier copy, and the warning goes away.
Note for testers: "Keep both" next to it is plain text, not a button. Say in your notes whether that seems right.

tests.title: Preview shows every step in order
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: Preview used to show only the open step; it now shows the whole playlist as readers will see it, starting at the open step.
steps: Open the **Note** step and change its text.
Without opening another step, choose **Preview** at the top.
Scroll up and down.
Choose **Edit** again, then open the Note + Scripture step and try the note editor's extras: select a word and use **Link to verse**, **Link to step** and **Embed passage**.
expected: Preview shows every step one after another, each as readers will see it, scrolled to the step you had open. Your changed note text is there.
The draft line under the title says **Draft · unsaved changes**.
A word linked to a verse or step shows as a link in the note; an embedded passage shows the verse text inside the note.

tests.title: Leaving or covering the editor keeps your draft
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: anything that covers the editor (Today, for example) now only hides it, and Discover offers to continue editing.
steps: Change the text of any open step but don't move to another step.
Choose the back arrow (‹) at the top left of the editor, and in the dialog choose the option that goes back to editing.
Now open **Today** from the app's menu, then go back to **Discover**.
expected: The back arrow shows a dialog about your unsaved changes instead of closing straight away, and going back from it brings the editor back with your change still there.
After visiting Today, Discover shows "You were editing Test playlist." with a **Continue editing** button, which reopens the editor with every step and your change still there.

tests.title: The review screen shows the steps and the checks
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: Review now shows the playlist as readers will see it, with all its steps, and no longer repeats the title and description fields.
tests.before: Use the playlist from the previous section. It should include a Video step with no transcript.
steps: Choose **Review & publish**.
Read the **Before you publish** list and scroll down through the steps.
Choose **Add one** (or **Fix**) next to the video transcript line.
expected: The screen shows the playlist's title and step count, "Who can open it: Anyone with a link" with a **Change** button, **Before you publish**, then "The steps as readers will see them" with every step in order. **Publish** is in the header and again at the end.
**Before you publish** includes lines such as "All passages found in …", a count of notes/questions/linked phrases, and "Video in step N has no transcript."
**Add one** takes you back to the editor with the video step open, where a **Transcript** box is available.

tests.title: Change who can open it from the review screen
steps: Add a transcript to the video step, then choose **Review & publish** again.
Choose **Change** next to "Who can open it".
On the details screen, choose **Only me**, then look at the review screen again (use the back arrow, then **Review & publish**).
Choose **Change** again, set it back to **Anyone with a link**, and return to the review screen.
expected: **Change** opens the **Playlist details** screen; its back arrow returns to the steps.
With **Only me** chosen, the review screen's button says **Save draft** instead of **Publish**.
With **Anyone with a link**, it says **Publish** again.

tests.title: Publish and find it again
steps: On the review screen, choose **Publish**.
Go back to **Discover** and find `Test playlist`, then open its options and choose **Edit playlist**.
expected: The button briefly says **Saving…**, then the editor closes and the playlist is saved.
The playlist appears in your list; editing it reopens the editor on its steps with every step and setting as you left them, and the draft line says **Draft · saved** with a time.

tests.title: Publish is blocked for an empty playlist
steps: Start a new playlist (**+ Create**, **Playlist**), type a title, choose **Next**, add no steps, and choose **Review & publish**.
expected: **Before you publish** says "Add at least one step before publishing." and the **Publish** button can't be pressed.
Leave this playlist without saving it.

sections.title: Playing a playlist on your own

tests.title: Scripture steps play in the reader with the playlist beside it
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: the framed passage block and the "End of passage" bar were removed from the reader.
steps: In **Discover**, open `Test playlist` and choose **Play playlist**.
Go to a scripture step (John 3:16-18).
expected: The side panel shows "Playlist · By <your name>" and the title, a progress bar, "Step N of M" and the current step highlighted in the queue.
The reader shows the passage marked with the reader's usual highlight. There is no frame around it, no "Step N · …" label, and no **End of passage** bar after it.
The step you marked **Leader only** is not in the queue when playing alone.

tests.title: Note, link, question, compare and video steps fill the screen
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: questions can show the author's answer, videos play at a normal 16:9 shape with the transcript folded underneath, and coming back to the playlist's tab brings the step back.
steps: Continue to the Note step, then the Question, Compare, Link and Video steps, using **Next step**.
On the Question step, type an answer in **Your response** and choose **Save response**, then choose **Show the author's answer**.
On the Compare step, choose **Open <passage> in a tab**, then click the playlist's own tab again.
On the Video step, look at the player's shape and open the transcript under it.
expected: These steps take over the reading area with a header ("Playlist · By … · N steps · ~X min"), a progress bar, an eyebrow like "Note · Step 3 of 8 · 1 min", **Previous** and **Next step** buttons, and an "Up next" line.
Saving the answer shows "Saved to your profile." and the message stays. The author's answer ("That God loves the world.") appears only after you ask for it, under "<your name>'s answer".
Compare shows both passages side by side; the tab button opens that passage in a new tab, and going back to the playlist's tab shows the Compare step again, not the bare reader.
The video is a normal widescreen shape, not squashed or overflowing, and its transcript shows when unfolded.
The **More** menu offers **Stop playlist**, which stops playing and returns to the reader.

tests.title: Listen reads scripture steps aloud
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: Listen used to read on past the passage when two steps were in the same chapter.
steps: While playing, choose the headphones button (**Listen**) in the Discover pane header.
Move to a scripture step that doesn't start at verse 1, and let it read to the end of the passage. Psalm 23:1-3 followed by another Psalm 23 step is a good case.
expected: The button shows as on (**Listening**) and narration starts at the passage's first verse, not at the start of the chapter.
At the end of the passage, the playlist moves on to the next step instead of reading on through the chapter.
Pressing the button again turns listening off.

tests.title: Finishing shows the completion screen
steps: Go to the last step and choose **Finish** (or **Finish playlist**).
expected: A **Playlist complete** screen shows how many steps and passages you went through and a **What you read** list, with **Share playlist** and **Done** buttons.
**Share playlist** copies the link and says so.

tests.title: Today offers to continue an unfinished playlist
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: the card's colours were fixed for dark mode.
steps: Play `Test playlist` again and stop part-way through (use **More**, then **Stop playlist**, on step 2 or 3).
Open **Today**. Look at it in both light and dark mode.
Choose **Resume**.
expected: Today shows a **Continue your playlist** card with the title, "Step N of M" and the step you were on. In dark mode its text is easy to read, like the Resume reading card above it.
**Resume** opens the playlist at that step, and only then closes Today.
After finishing the playlist, the card no longer appears on Today.

sections.title: Playing with a group
sections.intro: Needs two browsers or two devices.

setup.title: Prepare a second browser
setup.body: Open the preview link in a second browser, or a private/incognito window, signed in with a different account (or signed out, if joining a session allows it).

tests.title: Read with others takes the playlist into a session
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: Read with others used to start an empty shared session and leave the playlist behind.
steps: In the first browser, play `Test playlist` and go to step 2 or 3 (a Note or Question step).
Choose **Read with others** (on a narrow window it's under **More**).
Copy the invite link from the share window and open it in the second browser.
expected: A shared session starts with the playlist playing in it, on the same step you were on, and the share window opens on the session's invite link.
In the second browser, the same step shows. Book names show as words ("John 3"), not codes like "JHN 3", compare passages load, and **Read with others** isn't offered inside the session.

tests.title: The leader moves everyone; others say they're ready
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: the ready count now counts only readers, not the leader, and the leader can take everyone back a step.
steps: In the second browser, choose **I'm ready**.
In the leader's browser, choose **Move everyone to step N**.
In the leader's browser, choose **Move everyone back a step**.
expected: The leader's card says **Live · You're leading**; the other says **Live · Following <leader's name>**. The card looks the same on scripture steps (side panel) and on fullscreen steps.
With one reader ready, the count shows "1 of 1" (the leader isn't counted), and the chat says "Everyone is ready to move on".
Both browsers move to the next step, and the chat shows "<name> moved everyone to step N · <title>". Moving back takes both browsers back one step.
The **Leader only** step is part of the queue in the session.

tests.title: Shared answers and comments on verses
steps: On the Question step, in the second browser, write an answer, choose **Session** under **Who can see this**, and save it.
On a scripture step, in either browser, select a verse in the reader and choose **Comment in session** from the verse tools.
In the other browser, choose **Jump to verse** on that chat message.
expected: The leader sees the answer under **Group answers** ("1 shared"), and the chat shows "shared an answer" with "Asked: What stood out to you?".
The comment appears in the session chat attached to the verse (or phrase), and **Jump to verse** takes the reader there.

sections.title: On a phone
sections.intro: Use a real phone, or make the browser window narrower than 480 pixels.

tests.title: The phone editor shows the list or one step at a time
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: phones used to get an older one-column form; they now get the same editor as computers, one screen at a time.
steps: In **Discover**, choose **+ Create**, **Playlist**. Fill in a title and choose **Next**.
Choose **Add step** and add a scripture step for `John 3:16`.
Add a second step, a **Note**.
Tap the first step in the list, then use the bar's arrows and **All steps**.
expected: The details screen fits the phone, with a small cover thumbnail rather than a half-screen one.

In **Add a step**, the step types are one row of chips you can scroll sideways, and the chosen one stays in view; the step's fields show without scrolling past big cards. The passage box has a line of its own.
After adding a step, you go back to the step list with the new step in its place, ready to add the next.
Tapping a step shows that step with its settings below and a bar with **All steps**, "Step 1 of 2" and arrows for the previous and next step.
Choosing **Preview** shows every step in order in place of the list.

tests.title: Playing on a phone is compact
tests.why: Changed since commit `6a6cdd9`: phone playback was redesigned to take less of the screen.
steps: Play `Test playlist` on the phone.
On a scripture step, tap the step's title in the bar, then tap it again.
Move on to a Note or Question step, then open **More**.
expected: A scripture step is a slim bar above the chapter navigation, showing the step's title and place, **Previous**, **Next step** and **Listen**. A step without a note is just the bar, so the passage has the screen.
Tapping the title shows the author's note and "Up next"; tapping again folds it away. A step that has a note starts unfolded.
Note and Question steps have a one-line header with the playlist's name, and one row of buttons to move on, with Previous as an arrow.
There's no close (×) button to hit by mistake; **More** holds **Read with others** and **Stop playlist**. Nothing is cut off at the screen edges.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Reading plan editor still works, with items edited in place
steps: Open **Reading plans**, create or edit a reading plan, and add a scripture reading.
Use the reading's **Edit** button to change it, then save the plan.
expected: The reading opens for editing in place (the button is labeled "Edit <reading>", where it used to say "Preview"), and the change is saved.

tests.title: Playlists made here still open on the live site
tests.why: Commit `1acce9d` stores questions and compares so the current live Seed Bible can still read them. Earlier on this pull request, using this build broke the playlist list on the live site.
steps: After publishing `Test playlist` above, open https://seedbible.org in another tab, signed in with the same account.
Open **Discover** and play `Test playlist`.
expected: Your playlist list loads with no error, and `Test playlist` plays. The question shows as text, and the compare step shows its first passage.

tests.title: Dark mode
steps: Switch Seed Bible to dark mode and look at the details screen, the steps screen, the Add a step window, the Review & publish screen and a fullscreen Note step.
expected: All text is readable, with no white boxes or invisible text. On/off boxes (such as **Readers can share answers in group sessions** on a Question step) are full size and in the theme's colours.

notCovered: The large set of new and updated automated tests that came with this change.
The **Pause here for discussion** setting is saved with a step, but nothing in playback appears to use it yet, so there's nothing to check beyond the tick staying ticked.
Playlists saved with scenes on earlier test builds should still load with the scene headings skipped. Only someone who made one on an earlier build can check this.
The fix that stops two browser tabs from getting the same internal id. Its visible effect is covered by the Read with others test.
Translated (non-English) text: only the English wording was added, and translators will fill in the rest later.
Dropped since the last plan: tests for scenes, "Test with a group" and the old phone form with "Unsaved item changes". Those features were removed.
